title: QUIC long/short header
summary: QUIC packets use a variable-length header. Long headers (initial/handshake/0-RTT/retry) carry version and connection IDs; short headers (1-RTT) carry only the destination connection ID and packet number.

ext.summary: QUIC packets use a variable-length header. Long headers (initial/handshake/0-RTT/retry) carry version and connection IDs; short headers (1-RTT) carry only the destination connection ID and packet number.

structure.meaning: Always 1 (distinguishes QUIC from other protocols sharing the port).
QUIC version (0x00000001 for v1); 0x00000000 for version negotiation.
Connection IDs (0-20 bytes each) with length prefixes (long header only).
Encrypted/protected packet number; length signalled in flags (short) or derived (long).

ext.example_decoded: Long header, initial, version 1, empty DCID/SCID, token length 0
notes: QUIC runs over UDP; port 443 by default.
All packets after the initial are authenticated/encrypted with AEAD (TLS 1.3 keys).
Connection IDs allow migration across IP addresses.
Packet numbers are monotonically increasing per packet-number space (initial/handshake/application).
